content.intro: Learn content negotiation and request metadata through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Content Negotiation and Request Metadata matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines content negotiation and request metadata as part of middleware, cookies, sessions, and messaging. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Accept headers; Request content types; Handling JSON and HTML; HttpRequest metadata; Returning the correct response format. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Accept headers
items.text: Accept headers is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: Request content types
items.text: Request content types is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: Handling JSON and HTML
items.text: Handling JSON and HTML crosses an application boundary. Define the data contract, timeouts/failure behavior, authorization and retry/idempotency rules; verify with synthetic input and avoid live secrets in practice.

items.title: HttpRequest metadata
items.text: `HttpRequest` exposes method, path, query parameters, submitted form values, files, headers, cookies and user/session state when middleware is configured. Treat all externally supplied values as untrusted.

items.title: Returning the correct response format
items.text: Returning the correct response format shapes the presentation layer. Separate layout from business logic, escape untrusted output, provide meaningful empty/error states, and check semantic structure and keyboard usability.
